main_body: A wooden frame with a large yellow hide or mat stretched across it and tied with blue lashings. Brown side posts and a bottom beam sit on short legs.
top_band: none. Column x=15 shows a 1-row brown beam at row 1 (#845535), then the hide face (rows 2-16, L=186 to 154) with blue lashing rows interrupting it. There is no separate lighter horizontal band with a step below it.
evidence: The scan at x=7, 15 and 22 shows an outline at row 0, then a 1-row brown beam at row 1, then the hide panel running from rows 2 to 17. The hide is a vertical face drawn flat from the front, and its lightest rows (L=186) grade smoothly into the mid tones with no front-edge step. The top beam is only 1 px, which is a rim. The bottom beam at rows 17-19 is a 2-3 row front band of the same brown family, not a top surface. The side posts are flat vertical strips. No horizontal beam top or base top is visible from above, so the piece reads as a front elevation, or at best a flat slab seen from above. Both fail the contract.

style.evidence: The outline is a tinted dark brown (#22140d, 0% neutral edge pixels), so it is not a sticker line. The hide has about 4 tones (#d8bb68, #bc9a45, #9c7a30, #7b5c22), the wood has 3 and the blue lashing has 2-3. There are no 5x5 flat fills. Against that, the candidate has only 15 distinct colours versus 40 and 38 for the references, and its median of 12 colours per tile is below their 17 and 20. The hide texture is mostly bands of colour with few per-fibre dots, and the wood is smooth with little grain. It reads thinner than the stall and the well, so it fails when in doubt.
